newsitem.title: MEXICO: Opposition widens lead in poll for Mexico City vote.
newsitem.headline: Opposition widens lead in poll for Mexico City vote.

text.p: Mexico's main leftist party has extended its lead in the period preceding July's key race for Mexico City mayor, a newspaper poll said on Thursday.

The poll by Mexico City's Reforma newspaper showed Cuauhtemoc Cardenas, candidate for the Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD), with an 11 percentage point lead over his nearest rival, a conservative.
Cardenas, a former president's son who twice failed in his own bid for the post, garnered 35 percent support compared to 24 percent for National Action Party (PAN) candidate Carlos Castillo Peraza.
Ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) candidate Alfredo del Mazo trailed with 20 percent support.

The race for Mexico City, the first in modern times here, will be the most closely watched of July 6 mid-term elections because of the city's size and political weight. Previously, the sensitive post was appointed by the president from the ranks of the PRI.

The survey's results were similar to those in recent polls, although Cardenas' lead has grown compared to earlier Reforma polls. A March poll by the newspaper showed Cardenas with 29 percent support compared to 27 percent for Castillo Peraza.
The new poll was carried out on a sample of 1,000 voters from April 18-20 and had a margin of error of 3.1 percent.

It said Cardenas was viewed favourably by 53 percent of would-be voters while Castillo Peraza was seen as favourable by 35 percent. The PRI's Del Mazo was viewed favourably by 27 percent, but seen as unfavourable by 49 percent.
The poll indicated the candidate was seen as more important by voters than his political party and that Cardenas was seen as honest, capable and hard-working.
Analysts say the PAN, which was leading in polls until the parties chose their candidates three months ago, was hurt by its choice of Castillo Peraza, an acerbic former party leader.
